body:
Implements the audit-driven upgrade plan for the ar/en storefront in the agreed order: **P0 safety & clarity → P1 tangible UI upgrade → P2 measured motion**. Everything was verified with a real production build (`next build --webpack`) and measured in Chromium 153; a new E2E suite pins the acceptance criteria.

Full write-up with numbers: `docs/ui-upgrade-2026-09.md`.

## P0 — content is never blank
- **Root cause (measured):** the server HTML for `/ar` shipped **23 elements with `opacity:0`**, including the `template.tsx` wrapper around the entire page — a slow/failed hydration or a stalled `IntersectionObserver` meant a blank page, and no-JS meant no site.
- `Reveal` rewritten as progressive enhancement (no framer-motion): server HTML is fully visible (**0** inline `opacity:0` now); an element is hidden only after React has armed it *and* it is below the fold; one shared observer + a passive scroll sweep for instant jumps (End key / anchors); no-JS, reduced-motion and print are force-visible.
- Page transition is CSS keyframes, skips cart/checkout/account/login/register, and starts from a visible opacity — Chrome never counts content first painted at `opacity: 0` toward LCP, so the old 0→1 fade made the LCP element a 40px nav link.
- `CounterStats` renders the real values server-side (was "0"); hero entrance is CSS-only and does not wait for hydration.
- 44×44 touch targets (wishlist, add-to-cart, carousel controls, locale switcher, logo, breadcrumbs, filter pills); the header fits 375px (account/wishlist move to the bottom-nav "More" sheet on phones); bottom nav active state is no longer colour-only; `main` reserves tab-bar height + `safe-area-inset-bottom`.
- Decorative hero/listing images get `alt=""`; the product image has a described alt.
- Also fixed: a pre-existing base-ui Sheet trigger `data-slot` hydration mismatch and a CLS source (Alfasigma SVG declared with the wrong aspect ratio).

## P1 — UI upgrade (priority order from the plan)
1. Editorial hero: eyebrow, claim, lead, primary CTA (+ "Why trust us?" → `#trust`), three trust chips, product photo with clinical-evidence card and partner chip.
2. Proof strip with **verified numbers only** (2019 founded · 8 products · 2 core categories · NFSA valid through 2030) + documented partner marquee.
3. **Product Spotlight** (`product-spotlight.tsx`): one product at a time — who it's for, form, availability, price, key benefit, browse/request-info CTAs, RTL-aware arrows, thumbnails.
4. **Trust Journey** (`trust-journey.tsx`): four numbered steps with a scroll-driven progress rail (transform-only; fully drawn without JS / under reduced motion).
5. **Shop by Need** (`shop-by-need.tsx` + `lib/products/positioning.ts`): men's health, women's health, medical devices, dental care (coming soon, non-interactive); tiles link to `/products?need=…`.
6. Redesigned product cards: audience/category label, name, benefit, form, availability + price, CTA row, balanced hover — no text over the photo.
7. Evidence block: what "evidence-based" means, a **distinct reference count computed from catalog data**, and the official PDF leaflets. About page gets a principles band (clarity before marketing / evidence before claims / trust before selling). Listing gets need + category filters (3–4 total); PDP gallery is sticky on desktop.

## P2 — measured motion
Opacity/transform/clip-path only, visible fallbacks everywhere, a CSS scroll-driven parallax (`animation-timeline: view()`) on the story-band photo only, light page fade outside commerce flows. No WebGL, no cursor effects, no infinite scroll, no magnetic buttons beyond the single hero CTA.

## Measurements (production build, same machine, median of 5)
| Page / device | Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/ar` desktop 1440 | LCP | 1,136 ms (hero image after fade) | **340 ms** (hero image from first paint) |
| `/ar` desktop | LCP element Chrome sees | nav link, 1,890 px² | product image, 348,416 px² |
| `/ar` mobile 375, 4× CPU | LCP | 2,148 ms | **568 ms** |
| `/ar/products` mobile, 4× CPU | LCP | 1,736 ms | **500 ms** |
| `/ar` | CLS | 0.000 (everything hidden) | **0.000** |
| `/ar` mobile, 4× CPU | TBT (INP proxy) | 406 ms | 488 ms (+embla for the spotlight) |
| `/ar` at 300–600 ms, 4× CPU | painted text/link nodes | 0 / 62 | 81 / 81 |
| `/ar` server HTML | inline `opacity:0` | 23 | **0** |

## Tests
- `npm test` — 85 unit tests (incl. ar/en dictionary parity) ✅ · `npm run lint` ✅ · `tsc --noEmit` ✅ · `next build --webpack` ✅
- **New `e2e/visibility.spec.ts` (12 tests, all passing locally):** hero / product spotlight / trust & quality / CTA visible after load, after scrolling and after an instant jump to the bottom; JS disabled; observer never fires; hydration never happens; slow hydration; `prefers-reduced-motion` hides nothing; no horizontal overflow at 375/768/1440 in ar + en; primary mobile targets ≥ 44×44.
- `e2e/smoke.spec.ts` updated for the hero's new secondary CTA. The contact-form smoke test needs the Postgres/Payload backend (not available in the sandbox) — unchanged.

## Notes for review
- No new marketing/medical claims: every number is computed from the catalog or comes from facts already documented in the dictionary.
- `package-lock.json` is synced with the `bcrypt → npm:bcryptjs` override that `package.json` already declares.
- Dark hero / WebGL remain behind their env flags (off by default) and are untouched.

## CI status
- The three checks on this PR did **not run**: GitHub reports *"The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased"* (Actions billing on the account — nothing to do with the code). Re-run the checks once billing is sorted.
- Independently of that, `master`'s last run failed at **Install dependencies**: the committed lockfile was out of sync with the `bcrypt → npm:bcryptjs` override in `package.json`, so `npm ci` refuses to install (`EUSAGE … not in sync`). The lockfile sync in this PR fixes that — verified locally with `npm ci --dry-run` against both lockfiles.
title: Editorial medical commerce upgrade: visible-by-default reveals, spotlight, trust journey, shop by need
